exposure: nasopharyngeal microbiome composition (specifically Lactobacillus detection and abundance)
cohort: The study participants were 118 previously healthy, term infants who had confirmed acute respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) infection.
finding: The nasopharyngeal detection and increased abundance of Lactobacillus during RSV acute respiratory infection in infancy are associated with a reduced risk of childhood wheezing illnesses at age 2 years.
